citation.title: Discrete-time autoregressive model for unequally spaced time-series observations
citation.authors: Elorrieta, F.; Eyheramendy, S.; Palma, W.

topic: Complex irregular autoregressive (CIAR) model for unequally spaced time series. The model uses a state-space representation and Kalman filtering, and is applied to astronomical light curves.
own_question: Can a discrete-time irregular AR model capture negative as well as positive autocorrelation, and can it forecast unobserved points?
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors fit a complex AR(1) process with a latent imaginary part by Kalman-recursion maximum likelihood. Monte Carlo tests (n=300) use simulated irregular sampling. Applications are residuals of harmonic fits to OGLE/Hipparcos variable-star light curves. One-step forecasts with intervals are shown on an AGN K-band light curve, using an expanding window over the last 10%. The paper reports no fusion diagnostics, no exogenous inputs and no real-time timing.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: State-space autoregressive models with time-varying transition matrices can produce Kalman-filter one-step predictions and intervals for irregularly sampled series. In this model the prediction uncertainty depends on the time gap.
claim_checks.qualification: Univariate astronomy demonstration only. It is not evidence for CES nowcasting or for exogenous BES/ECEI inputs. The statement that intervals widen with gap size is the authors' observation about Fig. 7b and was not visually checked here.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Univariate only: past observations are used to forecast the next irregular observation. There are no exogenous inputs, and report-arrival latency is not modeled.
validation_if_relevant: Simulations, plus one expanding-window forecast on a single AGN light curve. No held-out-campaign analogue exists.
forbidden_inferences: The paper does not show the model suits plasma or CES data.
It does not show the model is causal-GP-equivalent or better than hold baselines for our task.
It does not demonstrate real-time feasibility.
It does not establish that irregular AR is standard in fusion.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Cite only optionally, in theoretical background, as an example of Kalman-based modeling of irregular sampling relevant to strictly past, irregular CES reports. It is not needed unless a state-space baseline is discussed. Our project did not implement it.
